_ruling: Ryan, 2026-09-07: every file in build/ that is not a store in the read model must be EXPLAINED here, not assumed. Four gates was never a magic number - it was how many properties needed checking at the time. This is the fifth.
_why: build_read_model.py reads a file only if it is a JSON object with a top-level `claims` list. Anything else it skipped in silence: no log, no count, no gate. A store that broke, was truncated, or was written in a shape the reader does not know would have vanished with the build still reporting success. Seventh instance of that defect across this project; the first six were found by accident.
_how_to_use: A file listed here is a file someone LOOKED AT and said is not a claim store. If G5 names a file that is not here, do not add it to make the gate pass - work out why it is not a store first. If G5 says a declared file has GROWN a claims list, the declaration is stale and the file is now a store the reader is dropping.

by_shape.why: the reader takes a JSON object with a `claims` list. A bare array is a worklist, a development dump or a game roster file - never a claim store in this archive.

clubs.why: the CLUB TABLE. The build reads it through paths.CLUBS as a table, not as claims.

person-merges.why: the merge DECLARATION. Read through paths.PERSON_MERGES and applied to identity, not ingested as claims.

club-key-normalisation.why: a decision record: which club keys were normalised, what was REFUSED, and when it was decided.

assistants-identity.why: a decision record for the assistants store's identity, carrying its ruling and its refusals.

coach-promotions.why: a decision record: which coaching seasons were promoted, what was left alone, and what it was checked against. Its claims reach the model through coach-seasons-promoted.

coach-demotions.why: a decision record and its leads.

officials-applied.why: a record of what the officials application did, including the dual-role men.

cfl1945-season-restore.why: a record of a restore: what was restored, what had no club in its record, which slugs did not match.

pfa-match.why: match leads: matched, unmatched, and leads. Evidence for a decision, not claims.

college-guides-candidates.why: candidate documents and the fields refused, before anything was ingested.

guide-prose-corpus-leads.why: 254 MB of leads for the prose corpus. The claims it led to are the guide-prose-corpus store.

guide-pre1950-delimited.status: RS-G5 fails on this file ON PURPOSE. The red is correct and MUST NOT be cleared.
guide-pre1950-delimited.why_it_is_not_here: Parsing owns that file and wrote the ruling into it: the 38-against-1,653 measurement, the unmapped-label vocabulary, and Fetching's sweep recording it as the only nested-claims file in all 1,146 build files. Restating any of that here would make two places able to say different things about one ruling - the defect this service spent 2026-09-07 removing twice (RS-G5's own copy of the reader's test; a duplicate readings.py that took the bio endpoint down). Read theirs.
guide-pre1950-delimited.what_this_gate_adds: only that the file is not a store in the read model and is not declared away here. The reason it is not declared away lives with Parsing.
guide-pre1950-delimited.for_whoever_arrives_in_a_hurry: Ryan's instruction: an unexplained red gets 'fixed' by someone in a hurry. This one is explained - in the file named above. Do not declare it here to make the gate green.

_bounded: Fetching's sweep of all 1,146 build files (2026-09-07) found guide-pre1950-delimited to be the only file holding claims below the top level, so RS-G5 has exactly one outstanding case rather than an unknown number. The measurement itself is recorded in dataset/declarations/guide-pre1950-delimited.json; it is referenced here, not restated.
